Frequently Asked Questions

Is a heat pump enough for Easley winters, or do I need backup heat?

A properly sized heat pump handles typical Upstate winters on its own, and modern units hold capacity well below freezing. Auxiliary electric strips cover the coldest snaps, and a dual fuel setup pairs the heat pump with a gas furnace for homes that want gas backup. The load calculation determines which configuration fits.

My drains clog every few months. Is repeated clearing the answer?

No, at that frequency the blockage has a structural cause. Recurring clogs usually trace to a bellied line, root intrusion, or buildup that clearing only punches through. A camera inspection finds the actual condition, and the repair gets quoted from what the camera shows.

Can my older Easley home’s panel handle a major appliance addition?

That is exactly what a panel evaluation answers. The electrician totals the existing load, measures what capacity remains, and states whether the addition fits or the panel needs upgrading first. Adding load to a panel at its limit trips breakers at best and overheats conductors at worst.

Why does my house still feel sticky when the AC is clearly running?

Cooling removes moisture only while the system runs, so an oversized unit that satisfies the thermostat quickly leaves humidity behind. Longer run cycles, correct sizing at replacement, or dedicated dehumidification each address it at different price points, and a diagnostic identifies which applies.

Which communities near Easley do you cover?

Coverage includes Liberty, Powdersville, and Piedmont, with the rest of the Upstate footprint behind them. Feel free to call if you’re unsure if we serve your home.
